newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes lower on exports and plantings.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes lower on exports and plantings.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on bearish export news, traders said.
USDA early Thursday said U.S. net export sales of corn during the week ended March 27 totaled 323,100 tonnes, below expectations for 450,000 to 600,000 tonnes.

Traders also said a sharp drop in the soybean complex lent pressure to the corn market as did a late fund-related break in wheat futures. Values in the soy pits also were hit by a lighter-than-expected weekly export sales number, the traders said.
Early seedings of corn in the U.S. were also cited.
"They're starting to plant in Indiana," said Brian Scott, vice-president of R.J. O'Brien. "We'd be planting here (in Illinois) if it weren't turning cold here next week."
"Corn is still overpriced at this level, given our stocks," Scott added.
Concerns continued to circulate about dwindling stocks of soybeans but U.S. corn and wheat stocks remain at generally "comfortable" levels, sources said.
Corn closed one to 7-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with May down 7-1/2 at $3.01.
The four- and 20-day moving averages (MA) for the May contract were giving off bullish signals early Thursday. The four-day MA for May was at $3.10 and the 20-day was at $3.04.

Technicians noted first support in the May at $3.06-1/2 and second support at $3.02. The session low for May was $3.00. First resistance was at $3.11-1/2 and second resistance was at $3.16. The session high for May was $3.06-1/2.
The nine-day relative strength index (RSI) for the May closed at 52 percent. The market generally views an RSI of 70 or more as overbought and 30 or less as oversold.

In spread trading, USA Trading did two million bushels of July/May at two cents per bushel, premium July, traders said. LFG Futures did four million bushels of July/May at two cents, premium July and Smith Barney spread 2.5 million July/December at 17-1/2 cents per bushel, premium July, floor sources said.

Fund selling in corn totaled roughly 10 million bushels with Goldenberg Hehmeyer selling four million of May, LFG Futures selling five million May and Iowa Grain selling two million bushels of May, traders said. Continental Grain bought two million July, one million May and four million bushels of December, traders said. Continental also sold four million bushels of May, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 75,000 contracts, below the 76,647 traded Wednesday.

In corn options, FIMAT Futures bought 700 July $3.00 puts at 10-3/4 cents and sold 700 July $3.10 puts at 16-1/2 cents, traders said. ADM Investor Services bought 500 May $2.90 calls at 17 cents and sold 500 July $3.10 calls at 12 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 19,000 contracts, below the 23,179 traded Wednesday.
